item.title: Stephen Colbert Avoids Directly Addressing Trump's Role in 'Late Show' Cancellation Following Emmy Victory
item.description: Stephen Colbert, the former host of 'The Late Show,' avoided directly addressing whether President Donald Trump played a role in the cancellation of his program following his Emmy win for Outstanding Variety Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards. The show, which aired its final episode in May 2026, won the award months after its cancellation. During a post-Emmy interview with CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister, Colbert repeatedly deflected questions about Trump's potential involvement, instead making jokes about the reporter's dress and claiming he was 'deaf on this ear.' The White House denied any involvement from Trump in the decision, with spokesperson Davis Ingle stating, 'Neither President Trump nor anyone else in the Administration had anything to do with this.' item.description: The Cleveland City Council adopted a resolution on Monday evening that humorously challenges President Donald Trump's recent executive order renaming Lake Ontario to 'Lake America.' Council member Kris Harsh, the resolution's sponsor, declared during the meeting, 'I feel emboldened to take the extraordinary step of renaming Lake Erie as the Gulf of Cleveland today.' The resolution, which passed 13-1, criticizes Trump's practice of renaming geographical features without historical or legal precedent, stating that his actions have 'opened the door for United States officials to rename other geography.' Harsh also criticized Google and Apple for updating their maps to reflect Trump's name changes, demanding that both companies 'recognize our sovereignty.' The resolution, while not legally binding, serves as a satirical response to Trump's renaming efforts. item.title: Israel and Saudi Arabia Hold Intelligence Talks to Counter Houthi Threats
item.description: Regional diplomats have confirmed that Israel and Saudi Arabia are engaged in intelligence-sharing discussions mediated by the US Central Command (CENTCOM) to bolster Saudi defenses against escalating Houthi attacks. The talks, which followed a meeting between US CENTCOM Chief Admiral Brad Cooper and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, aim to provide Riyadh with critical intelligence to counter Houthi military operations. The Houthis have intensified their attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including a drone strike on oil pipelines and facilities, causing partial shutdowns, and an attack on civilians near the Yemen-Saudi border. Additionally, the Houthi forces have seized strategic islands in the Red Sea, blocking Saudi vessels from passing through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, effectively imposing an economic and diplomatic blockade on Saudi Arabia. item.description: During a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Tuesday, Senator Mazie Hirono (D-HI) delivered a scathing critique of FBI Director Kash Patel, accusing him of multiple failures in leadership and transparency. Hirono specifically highlighted Patel's alleged drinking problems, stating, 'You have been so drunk that briefings have been rescheduled so you could sleep it off,' and noted that Patel had agreed to take an alcoholism test following a challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen but had not yet released the results. She criticized Patel for lowering FBI hiring standards to allow applicants with a history of theft to join the agency, questioning why an organization tasked with investigating theft would hire individuals with such backgrounds. item.title: Trump's Convention Speech Ratings Fall Short of NFL Game Viewership
item.description: President Donald Trump's claim that his keynote speech at the Republican Party's midterm convention outperformed NFL game viewership was debunked by Nielsen ratings data. The NFL opener between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks drew over 25 million viewers, while Trump's speech at the convention in Dallas attracted approximately 3 million viewers. Trump had previously boasted on Truth Social about the convention's success, claiming it was 'a major, sold out hit, far bigger, better, and more important than anyone thought possible,' and that it 'beat the NFL' in viewership. However, the actual Nielsen numbers revealed a significant disparity, with the NFL game far surpassing the convention speech in audience size. item.title: Republican Congressman Proposes Impeachment of Defense Secretary Over Civilian Casualties in Iran
item.description: On September 15, 2026, Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY) introduced an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of being responsible for the deaths and injuries of over 200 civilians during a military operation in Iran. Massie's resolution, read on the House floor, detailed how Hegseth had deliberately degraded the legal review system meant to protect civilians during U.S. military operations. Specifically, Massie cited an incident at Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran, where more than 200 civilians were killed or injured due to Defense Department actions directed by Hegseth. The Kentucky Republican argued that Hegseth's policies fostered a 'war-making culture' within the Department of Defense, dismissing 'stupid rules of engagement' in favor of 'maximum lethality, not tepid legality.' item.title: Federal Judge Blocks Kennedy Center from Restoring Trump's Name on Building Exterior
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts cannot honor President Donald Trump with an inscription on the building's exterior. U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper issued the ruling on Tuesday, blocking the president's hand-picked board from restoring Trump's name after an earlier order forced its removal. The judge stated that the board cannot install memorials for Trump or anyone else without Congress's approval, emphasizing that the board's resolution violates a federal court order and a statute enacted by Congress. The Kennedy Center's board had initially added Trump's name to the building's formal title in December 2025, crediting him with securing $257 million for a renovation. However, Judge Cooper ruled in May that the renaming was unlawful, as only Congress has the authority to authorize such changes, and ordered the removal of the name. item.title: Study reveals FOXA1-CYP4Z1 axis as key regulator in breast cancer lipid metabolism
item.description: A recent study published in Scientific Reports has uncovered a significant molecular mechanism in breast cancer progression involving the FOXA1-CYP4Z1 axis. The research demonstrates that FOXA1, a transcription factor, suppresses breast cancer development by downregulating CYP4Z1, a member of the cytochrome P450 family. CYP4Z1 was found to be markedly overexpressed in breast cancer tissues and strongly correlated with poor patient prognosis. Functional experiments showed that silencing CYP4Z1 inhibited cancer cell proliferation, migration, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition while promoting apoptosis and senescence. Conversely, overexpression of CYP4Z1 enhanced malignant behaviors in breast cancer cells. Lipidomics analysis revealed that CYP4Z1 downregulation disrupted lipid homeostasis, particularly by inducing triglyceride accumulation, highlighting its critical role in maintaining tumor lipid metabolism. item.title: Israel's Far Right Proposes Seven-Year Plan for Gaza Displacement
item.description: Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the Jewish Power party, has unveiled a seven-year plan called 'Disengagement 710' aimed at facilitating the 'voluntary migration' of Gaza's population to countries such as Turkey, Ethiopia, and Congo. The plan calls for the departure of approximately 250,000 people in the first year, 1.11 million within three years, and 1.86 million within seven years, which would encompass most of Gaza's population. Ben-Gvir's proposal includes creating a new ministry dedicated to 'voluntary migration,' complete with a minister, director-general, budget, and international negotiating team. The plan is presented as a solution to the ongoing conflict, with Ben-Gvir stating, 'Instead of illusions of peace now, we need actions of emigration now.' However, Gazans interviewed by RT reject the initiative as illegal under international law and a crime against humanity. item.title: FBI Records Reveal Anonymous Donor Paid for Cremation of Trump Attempted Assassin
item.description: The New York Post reported that an 'anonymous donor' paid for the cremation of Thomas Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate former President Donald Trump at a July 2024 rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. This detail was buried in documents provided to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA) as part of his inquiry into the assassination attempt. The documents included a note at the end of an FBI interview summary with Crooks' father, Matthew Crooks, indicating that an anonymous donor covered the cremation costs. Matthew Crooks, described as retired and his wife on leave from work, reportedly lacked the financial means for funeral arrangements. Matthew also stated he was unemployed at the time of the shooting. The revelation was first made public in 2024 by Rep. item.title: US AI Labs Face Debate Over Distilling Frontier Models for Smaller, More Efficient Systems
item.description: The article discusses a debate within the AI community regarding whether US-based open-weight AI labs should be allowed to distill frontier models to create smaller, more efficient models. The controversy arises as frontier AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are pushing back against the practice of distilling their models, calling it 'illicit' and 'theft,' while simultaneously using similar techniques themselves. The article highlights that distillation is a common practice in AI development, where smaller models are trained using the outputs of larger models. This process, known as model distillation, is seen as a way to make AI more accessible and efficient. However, frontier labs argue that distillation violates their terms of service and could lead to security risks. item.title: Trump Claims Security Guard Avoided Death in Kennedy Center Ceiling Collapse During Renovation Push
item.description: President Donald Trump has continued his campaign to gain more control over the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, claiming that a security guard narrowly avoided death due to the building's poor condition. The incident in question involved a small section of ceiling collapsing in a heavily trafficked hallway at the Kennedy Center earlier this month, though no injuries were reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick initially stated that the ceiling fragment had 'missed one of the Center's security guards by just minutes' and could have 'killed' numerous patrons. Trump expanded on this claim in a lengthy post on his social media platform, Truth Social, where he argued that the building's state of disrepair necessitated his increased involvement in its management. item.title: FBI Director Kash Patel Faces Scrutiny Over Claimed Statistics on Crime Reduction
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel faced criticism during a congressional hearing for citing statistics that former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe and CNN's Evan Perez described as questionable. Patel, President Donald Trump's nominee, presented data to counter Democratic criticism of his leadership, but McCabe and Perez questioned the validity of the numbers, particularly regarding the FBI's role in reducing crime rates. McCabe noted that many of the statistics Patel referenced, such as a 500 percent increase in enforcement actions and claims of 1,100 thwarted terrorist attacks, were not accurate or within the FBI's jurisdiction. Perez highlighted that some statistics, like declining carjacking rates, do not fall under the FBI's core responsibilities, making it inappropriate for the FBI to claim credit for such trends. item.title: How to Accurately Compare Google Trends Data in Spreadsheets Without Misinterpreting Search Interest
item.description: The article discusses a method for comparing Google Trends data in spreadsheets without confusing relative interest scores with actual search volumes. The author, who is building a tool called CleanScrape, explains that a Google Trends value of 100 does not represent 100 searches but rather a relative interest score within the comparison. The article provides a step-by-step guide using an Apify Actor to extract Google Trends data for terms like 'ChatGPT' and 'Claude' in the US over a three-month period. The process involves inputting specific JSON parameters to request interest-over-time data, which is then exported as a CSV or Excel file. The author emphasizes the importance of keeping both search terms in the same request to avoid separately normalized series that would make comparisons difficult. item.title: Police Departments Use Flock Surveillance System with Inappropriate Search Reasons
item.description:
According to a report by 404 Media and the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), law enforcement officers across multiple jurisdictions have been using Flock's surveillance search engine to track license plates and locations with inappropriate, nonsensical, or humorous reasons. The EFF's analysis revealed that officers frequently entered phrases such as 'LMAO,' 'IDK,' 'Hehe,' 'Asdfg,' 'dickhead,' 'shithead,' and even 'robbery I don't remember the case number leave me alone' into the 'reason' field when conducting searches. Some officers simply left the field blank or used generic terms like 'investigation' or 'test.'
The report highlights that these searches were conducted across more than 19,000 cameras in 1,558 cities and towns, with records showing hundreds of thousands of searches performed. item.title: Flow Neuroscience's FDA-Approved Headset Offers Non-Pharmaceutical Depression Treatment in US
item.description: Flow Neuroscience has launched its FDA-approved headset for depression treatment in the United States, marking a significant development in mental health care. The device, which delivers low-intensity electrical stimulation to the left frontal lobe of the brain, is designed to be used at home for 30 minutes daily via a mobile app. This approach targets the same brain region affected in depression, where reduced activity and weaker neural connections are common. The device received FDA approval in December 2025, positioning it as an alternative to traditional antidepressant medications, which are taken by approximately one in six American adults. While the device costs $2,200 for a 10-week treatment period followed by $325 monthly thereafter, it offers a non-pharmaceutical option that could potentially reduce reliance on antidepressants. item.title: CBS News' '60 Minutes' Premiere Shows Significant Viewership Decline Under New Editor-in-Chief
item.description: The premiere of CBS News' '60 Minutes' for its first full season under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss has shown a significant decline in viewership compared to previous years. According to early Nielsen data reported by the New York Post, the show drew approximately 7.7 million viewers for its season opener, marking the smallest premiere audience since at least 2000. This represents a 19 percent drop in total viewership and a 33 percent decline in the key 25-to-54 demographic compared to the previous year's premiere. CNN's Brian Stelter reported on BlueSky that preliminary numbers indicate the premiere could be down more than 20 percent year-over-year, with the previous season's premiere drawing 10 million viewers. A TV executive cited a weaker NFL lead-in this year and Nielsen methodology changes as contributing factors, though the executive noted it would still be 'a pretty striking drop.' item.description: During a House Financial Services Committee hearing on September 15, 2026, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faced intense questioning from Ranking Member Maxine Waters (D-CA) regarding inflation and fiscal policy. Waters pressed Bessent for direct answers on whether tariffs have contributed to rising inflation, asking, 'If tariffs are not inflationary, as you claimed in your previous testimony, then why has inflation increased by more than 3% over the past year?' Bessent repeatedly avoided providing a clear response, leading to a heated exchange where he snapped, 'You're not making sense!' Waters, who was given the floor for her five-minute questioning period, continued to challenge Bessent on the administration's economic policies, particularly the record $40 trillion national debt under President Trump's leadership. item.title: Roman Empire's Road Network Reveals Other Cities Were Better Connected Than Rome
item.description: A new study published in Nature Communications on September 15, 2026, challenges the common saying that 'all roads lead to Rome.' Researchers from Aarhus University in Denmark, led by Professor Tom Brughmans, have conducted extensive research on the Roman Empire's road system, revealing that several other cities were better connected by road than Rome itself. The study, part of a larger digital atlas project called 'Itiner-e,' mapped nearly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) of Roman roads. The findings indicate that major cities like Antioch, Ancyra (modern-day Ankara), Byzantium (modern-day Istanbul), and Corinth were better connected to the road network than Rome. The research identified the empire's 'most important intermediary route' by land, which did not run through Rome but followed the North African and Levantine coast past Antioch and near Ankara, crossed over to Europe at Constantinople, and moved through the Po Valley and Milan into France. item.title: Former TikTok Executives Launch AI-Powered App to Guide Users in Taking Better Selfies
item.description: A new iOS application called Superpose, developed by former TikTok executives Melody Chu and Jing Liu, has been launched to help users improve their photography skills through AI guidance. The app, which was released in July 2026, allows users to take selfies or photos of friends and generates four AI-assisted pose suggestions. Users can save these poses or use the 'match pose' feature to align themselves with the suggested framing. The app offers five free pose generations per day, with additional packs available for purchase at $2.99 for five or $9.99 for 20. Chu, who previously worked at Meta, TikTok, and Slack, explained that the idea stemmed from her personal frustration with her husband's poor photography skills. She aimed to solve this problem using advancements in computer vision and generative AI. Superpose has already been downloaded over 22,000 times, with users generating more than 190,000 poses. item.title: Orange County Holds First-Ever E-Bike Buyback Event Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: Orange County authorities recently held a groundbreaking e-bike buyback event, modeled after gun buyback programs, which drew significant public interest and some criticism. The event, organized by the Orange County district attorney’s office, offered gift cards ranging from $200 to $1,000 for surrendered e-bikes, e-scooters, and e-motorcycles. Nearly 1,000 vehicles were collected, filling nine 26-foot U-Haul trucks, with participants lining up as early as midnight. The program, funded by asset forfeiture funds and an additional $5,000 from Orange County Supervisor Katrina Foley, aimed to remove potentially dangerous e-bikes from the streets. District Attorney Todd Spitzer emphasized that the initiative was part of a broader strategy to address e-bike-related safety issues, including child endangerment charges against parents who allowed underage riders to use inappropriate e-motorcycles. item.title: Wichita Bombardier Employees Resist Trump's Threat to Ban Canadian Jet Manufacturer Sales
item.description: Wichita, Kansas - Three days after President Donald Trump threatened to ban sales of Canadian jet manufacturer Bombardier in the United States, employees at the company's U.S. headquarters in Wichita expressed strong opposition to the president's remarks. An employee, who wished to remain anonymous, walked out of the company's headquarters and spoke to a reporter after ensuring no one was nearby. The employee stated that the president's comments felt like a betrayal of American workers, particularly in a state that has historically supported Republican candidates. The Washington Post article, published on September 14, 2026, highlights the backlash from Bombardier workers in Wichita, a city known for its significant aerospace industry presence. The exchange occurred after a grilling from Senator Dick Durbin (D-IL) on the topic. Senator Kennedy expressed confusion about why bestiality was being discussed in the context of hiring FBI agents, stating that such issues have 'really hurt the FBI' by creating perceptions that political views matter more than qualifications. item.title: Trump's Arctic Commission Chair Raises Conflicts of Interest and Foreign Policy Concerns
item.description: The U.S. Arctic Research Commission, which has historically advised Congress and the president on Arctic research and policy, has become a focal point of controversy following President Donald Trump's appointment of Thomas Dans, a Texas venture capitalist and MAGA influencer with no scientific background, as its chair. Dans, who has no formal expertise in Arctic science or policy, has leveraged his position to advance personal business interests, particularly with Damen Shipyards, a Dutch shipbuilder with which he has a prior business relationship. His advocacy for Damen's icebreaker projects, including a potential U.S. government contract, has raised ethical concerns, as Dans is not required to disclose conflicts of interest under federal ethics rules due to his non-employee status. The White House has defended Dans, stating he is "doing a great job" and that his shipbuilding expertise benefits the commission. item.title: Cher, Elton John and other stars pay tribute to legendary designer Bob Mackie
item.description:
Legendary costume and fashion designer Bob Mackie has died at age 87, prompting tributes from generations of entertainers whose careers and public images were shaped by his work. Cher, Elton John, Miley Cyrus, Sabrina Carpenter and Pink were among the stars who publicly honored the designer, whose glamorous creations became a defining part of American entertainment and popular culture.
Known as the “Sultan of Sequins,” Mackie was celebrated for elaborate costumes featuring sequins, feathers, beads, rhinestones and dramatic silhouettes. His long career included collaborations with some of the biggest names in music and television, including Dolly Parton, Tina Turner, Diana Ross, Madonna, Beyoncé and Pink. He also designed costumes for The Carol Burnett Show throughout its 11-year run from 1967 to 1978 and created distinctive fashions for Barbie dolls beginning in the late 1980s.

item.title: Economic analysts warn of potential US market crash due to Middle East tensions and AI sector slowdown
item.description: Political analysts Krystal Ball and Saagar Enjeti have raised concerns about an imminent U.S. economic downturn, citing a combination of Middle East geopolitical tensions and a potential slowdown in the artificial intelligence sector. The analysts highlighted recent developments in the Middle East, including the Houthis gaining control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait—a critical global shipping route—and damage to the Saudi Arabian East-West oil pipeline, which threatens 4% of global oil supply. These developments have contributed to surging oil prices, described by Ball as 'extraordinarily dire,' amid ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Enjeti warned that the U.S. economy, heavily reliant on AI-driven tech investments accounting for about half of real GDP growth since 2025, faces a potential 'freefall' if the AI industry slows down while inflation from Middle East conflicts continues to rise. The analysts noted that gasoline prices have reached $4.31 per gallon, with diesel at $6.

item.title: Family Corrects Misrepresentation of Victim in Beverly Hills Alley Murder Case
item.description: Vanik Voskanyan, a 40-year-old man from Yerevan, Armenia, was fatally stabbed in an alley behind the 400 block of North Palm Drive in Beverly Hills on the night of August 30, 2026. According to Beverly Hills police and the L.A. County medical examiner, Voskanyan died from multiple sharp-force injuries in a hospital shortly after the attack. The suspected assailant, 19-year-old Conoray Lawantara, a Beverly Hills resident, was charged with murder and pleaded not guilty. Lawantara claimed he acted in self-defense, stating he used a 3.9-inch knife after Voskanyan allegedly reached for his neck during a verbal altercation. However, Judge Keith Schwartz criticized the defense, noting that Lawantara 'stabbed him repeatedly, like in a horror movie,' and questioned why he confronted Voskanyan in the first place. item.title: Math Professor Claims OpenAI Used His Research Without Permission, Questions Value of Academic Competition in AI Era
item.description: A New York University mathematics professor, Tristan Buckmaster, has accused OpenAI of copying his work on a fluid dynamics equation, specifically the Euler problem, which is a stepping stone to solving the Navier-Stokes problem. Buckmaster, who was collaborating with Levent Alpöge from Anthropic, claims that OpenAI scientists approached him to jointly announce a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem after becoming aware of his research. He questions how OpenAI could have solved the problem so quickly, noting that the timing coincided with their awareness of his work. OpenAI's website announcement credited their AI model Astra with solving the Navier-Stokes proof, stating no user data was incorporated, though they acknowledged anonymized data might have been used to improve their models. Buckmaster expressed frustration that OpenAI did not answer his questions about whether their AI systems had access to his research. item.title: Fay Wray’s 1920s Fashion: A Study of Hollywood’s Transition from Flapper to Elegant Silhouettes
item.description: The article presents a collection of 40 vintage photographs showcasing the fashion styles of Canadian-American actress Fay Wray during the late 1920s. Wray, who would later become famous for her role in the 1933 film 'King Kong,' was a brunette starlet under contract with Paramount Pictures during this period. The photographs highlight her signature style that captured the transition of fashion in the late 1920s (1928-1929), where silhouettes began shifting from the boxy shapes of the mid-1920s to more fluid, elongated elegance. Wray's wardrobe featured classic late-1920s gowns with dropped waistlines, delicate silk crepes, satin, and soft pleating. As the decade closed, her style evolved toward bias-cut gowns that hugged natural curves while maintaining an elongated line. Her signature look included ultra-fitted cloche hats pulled low over the brow, often embellished with fabric flowers or subtle metallic brooches. item.title: Trump Criticizes Supreme Court Rulings on Mail-in Voting and Other Policies
item.description: President Donald Trump has publicly criticized the U.S. Supreme Court for its recent rulings, particularly regarding mail-in voting regulations, in a 463-word post on Truth Social. The president accused the justices of political cowardice and claimed the court's decisions have set America back 'at least a hundred years.' Trump specifically referenced the court's third ruling against his mail-in voting order, which blocked a U.S. Postal Service rule requiring new mail-in ballot verification procedures ahead of the November midterm elections. He argued that the court's decision was based on insufficient time to implement changes, calling the current mail-in voting system a 'totally CORRUPT and out of control Mail-In voting 'disaster,' which is a laughing stock all over the World.' Trump praised Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas for their dissent but questioned the loyalty of three justices he nominated during his first term. item.title: Melania Trump Denies Involvement in Don Jr.'s Wedding Finances Amid Russian Oligarch Scandal
item.description: First Lady Melania Trump has distanced herself from reports that a Russian oligarch, Umar Kremlev, helped finance the wedding of her son Donald Trump Jr. and his second wife, Bettina Anderson. According to a statement from Melania's representatives to The Daily Mail, she has no relationship with Kremlev and played no role in organizing the wedding or its financial planning. The wedding, held in Palm Beach, Florida, in late May, included a private island celebration in the Bahamas, with Kremlev reportedly contributing hundreds of thousands of dollars. Kremlev, a close associate of Russian President Vladimir Putin and president of the International Boxing Association, has been accused of facilitating the abduction of Ukrainian children, an issue that is personally significant to Melania. item.title: Photographer Luca Battaglia Captures Ethereal Carousel Scenes Through Long Exposures
item.description: The article discusses photographer Luca Battaglia's series titled 'Ticket non remboursable' (Non-Refundable Ticket), which captures traditional carousels across European city squares through long exposure photography. Battaglia uses heavy neutral density filters and exposures lasting up to 30 seconds to create ethereal images where the carousels blur into radiant bands of color and light while the surrounding city remains sharp and still. The article explains that Battaglia's work is deeply personal, as he grew up in Milan with fond memories of a neighborhood carousel that eventually disappeared. He began seeking out carousels not just as nostalgic attractions but as living hubs of memory and shared public life. The photographs show carousels in various European cities including Honfleur, Toulouse, Bercy in Paris, Deauville, Tikkimäki, Dijon, Tuileries in Paris, Grenoble, Charles Michels in Paris, Nice, and Marseille. item.title: FBI Documents Reveal Strange Behavior and Obsession with Firearms of Trump Assassin Attempter
item.description: Newly disclosed FBI documents, provided to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA) as part of his inquiry into the July 2024 shooting in Butler, Pennsylvania, detail years of increasingly strange behavior by Thomas Matthew Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate President Donald Trump. The records include FBI interviews with Crooks' father, Matthew, who described his son as emotionally distant, rarely laughing or showing strong feelings. Thomas developed an obsession with firearms and long-distance shooting during the pandemic, initially being a poor shot but improving over four to five years of practice. He used a pseudonym 'Bob Dole' to purchase rifle parts on Amazon, employed VPN and encrypted email services, and built a Glock 19-style handgun with a 3D printer, firing it only once before his father intervened. item.title: Accenture settles U.S. government DEI allegations with $25 million payment
item.description: Accenture, an IT consulting firm, has agreed to pay $25 million to settle allegations from the U.S. government regarding its diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices. The settlement, announced on Monday, involves the U.S. Department of Justice and Accenture, and specifies that the company will pay $25,000,000, including civil penalties and interest at a rate of 4% per annum from September 9, 2026. The Trump administration has targeted DEI practices in its second term, penalizing both public and private organizations for diversity initiatives that civil rights advocates argue help address historic inequities for marginalized groups such as women, the LGBT community, and ethnic minorities. The White House has characterized DEI as anti-merit and discriminatory against white people and men, leading to executive orders requiring federal contractors to eliminate DEI programs. item.title: New World Screwworm Returns to U.S., Threatening Livestock and Wildlife
item.description: The New World screwworm, a flesh-eating parasite that was eradicated from the United States in the 1950s, has made a comeback, reaching Texas and New Mexico. This parasitic fly's larvae feed on living tissue, causing severe wounds in livestock, wildlife, pets, and occasionally humans. The University of California San Diego, in collaboration with the County of San Diego Health and Human Services Agency, has developed a new tracking dashboard to predict where the parasite might strike next. The dashboard integrates confirmed detections, environmental conditions, and media reports to provide real-time risk assessments for counties across the country. Public health officials are concerned about the rapid spread of the parasite, which has been moving northward faster than anticipated. The U.S. Department of Agriculture is leading an eradication campaign using the sterile insect technique, which was successfully employed decades ago to eliminate the parasite. item.title: Nike-Backed CoachingHER Program Under Scrutiny for Gender Bias Training and Inclusive Definition of 'Girls'
item.description: The CoachingHER program, developed in partnership with Nike and the Tucker Center for Research on Girls & Women in Sport at the University of Minnesota, is facing increased scrutiny over its definition of 'girls' and its focus on gender bias training for coaches. Launched in 2023, the program aims to help coaches recognize unconscious gender biases and stereotypes that negatively affect girls' experiences in sports. However, a former coach, Sarah Barker, who created The Female Category, has raised concerns about the program's approach. Barker discovered that CoachingHER defines 'girls' as anyone under 18 who identifies as a girl, including transgender athletes, which she argues contradicts the program's stated mission of keeping girls in sports. The program's FAQ states that 'girls' includes those 'assigned female at birth or who identifies as a girl,' and emphasizes inclusivity of gender-expansive identities. item.title: Senate Bill Aims to Regulate Cryptocurrency Sector Amid Trump Family Wealth Concerns
item.description: The U.S. Senate is preparing to vote on the Clarity Act, a bill designed to regulate the cryptocurrency sector, which has reportedly generated over $1.4 billion for the Trump family in 2025 alone. Critics argue that the legislation fails to address potential conflicts of interest and could even facilitate further enrichment for the Trump family through their crypto ventures. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) criticized the bill on the Senate floor, calling its ethics provisions a 'fig leaf' that would not prevent Trump from making additional profits. The bill's critics, including Mark Hays of the Cryptocurrency and Financial Technology department, warn that the legislation would not rein in Trump's self-enrichment from crypto ventures and could 'supercharge' it. item.title: Penang Mandates Covered Walkways for Transit-Oriented Development Projects
item.description: Penang developers are now required to construct covered walkways and pedestrian links around transit stations under new regulations aimed at prioritizing public access and connectivity over property density. Jason H'ng Mooi Lye, chairman of Penang's local government and town and country planning committee, emphasized that Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) does not permit developers to seek higher density or plot ratios. Instead, TOD focuses on creating connectivity and essential public facilities to ensure easy access to LRT stations, bus stops, taxi stands, and other future transit infrastructure. H'ng highlighted that Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has already implemented covered walkway requirements for certain developments, even outside designated TOD zones, to address existing connectivity gaps. item.title: Democrats Expand Recruitment Program to Include Independent Candidate in Alaska
item.description: With less than 50 days until Election Day, House Democrats are adding new candidates to their top recruits list — including one who isn't actually a Democrat. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) announced Tuesday that it is expanding its 'Red to Blue' program, which offers candidates strategic guidance, staffing, and fundraising help, to include Bill Hill, an independent running for Alaska's at-large House seat, along with Michigan Democrat Will Lawrence and Wisconsin Democrat Mitchell Berman. The additions bring the program's total to 40 candidates for the cycle. Hill, a fisherman and former school superintendent, finished second behind the Republican incumbent in Alaska's nonpartisan primary and won the state Democratic Party's endorsement after committing to support organized labor and abortion rights. item.title: Bodega Peptides Tested Fail to Contain Actual Peptide Ingredients
item.description: WIRED conducted an investigation into the peptide products sold at bodegas, particularly focusing on the viral trend of peptides marketed for various health benefits. The publication purchased four types of peptides from Mr. Green, a Brooklyn bodega, and sent them to an independent testing lab. The results revealed that the samples did not contain the active peptide ingredients listed on their labels. Instead, the vials were found to be mislabeled or degraded, containing little more than water or saline solution. The testing showed low levels of heavy metals and endotoxins, suggesting they were not actively harmful, but the absence of the claimed ingredients meant the products were ineffective. The peptides market has surged in popularity, fueled by endorsements from figures like Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Joe Rogan, despite many of these substances not undergoing proper regulatory approval. item.description: The 2026 Emmy Awards ceremony, held at Los Angeles' Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026, saw 'Widow's Bay' dominate with 14 wins, including Outstanding Comedy Series. The Game of Thrones spin-off 'A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms' received only one award (Outstanding Stunt Performance) out of eight nominations, with fans expressing disappointment over the lack of recognition. item.description: According to a new book by Jacob Weisberg, former Slate editor and CEO, George W. Bush has secretly painted an unflattering portrait of Donald Trump, which he refuses to show to the public. Weisberg's book, 'Profiles in Cowardice: A Study of Collaboration in the Trump Era,' argues that Bush is among Trump's enablers not because of what he has done, but because of what he has not done. item.description: U.S. Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) returned to the Senate on Monday, September 14, 2026, after a nearly three-month absence due to a health-related issue. The Kentucky Republican had been hospitalized in June following a fall, which he claimed was the cause of his absence. However, reports indicate he was found unconscious at home and received CPR, leading to speculation about the severity of his condition. item.title: Gillibrand Pushes for More Federal Research and Better Care for Menopause
item.description:
Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Democrat of New York and chairwoman of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, is using a Senate hearing to push menopause higher on the federal health policy agenda. The hearing, titled “Half the Country, Zero Hearings: Meeting the Moment to End the Menopause Care Gap in America,” is scheduled to focus on the lack of research, medical training and effective care available to millions of women.
Gillibrand argues that menopause has been substantially under-researched and underfunded, despite the severity of symptoms that some women experience. She has described problems ranging from debilitating pain and heavy bleeding to mood changes and other symptoms that can interfere with daily life and work. She plans to use the hearing to advocate for additional federal funding for menopause research and bipartisan legislation addressing the research gap. item.title: Volkswagen's Mission Efficiency Concept Emphasizes Aerodynamic Efficiency Over Battery Size
item.description: Volkswagen has introduced the Mission Efficiency concept, which represents a departure from the current trend of large, heavy electric SUVs. The concept draws inspiration from the 2013 XL1 model, focusing on aerodynamic efficiency and minimalist design. The Mission Efficiency features a drag coefficient of 0.158, one of the lowest in the automotive industry, achieved through smooth organic contours, covered rear wheel wells, flush glazing, and a tapered teardrop profile. Unlike the original XL1, which was a two-seater priced for a niche market, the Mission Efficiency is designed to accommodate four adults within a compact footprint using standard MEB+ architecture. Apple TV's 'Widow's Bay' followed with 19 nominations, and 'Pluribus' received 18. item.title: Correcting the Typography of Botanical Names on Websites
item.description: The article discusses a common mistake in how websites format botanical names, specifically the incorrect use of italics. Most websites wrap entire plant names in italics, but according to botanical naming conventions (ICN for wild plants and ICNCP for cultivated ones), only certain parts should be italicized. The genus, species epithet, and infraspecific epithets should be italicized, while rank markers (such as subsp., var., f.), author citations, hybrid signs (×), cultivar groups, and cultivar names (which go in single quotes) should not be italicized. For example, 'Hosta 'Blue Angel'' should be formatted as Hosta 'Blue Angel' with only 'Hosta' italicized. The author noticed this error on their plant app, PlantGeekz, while building a library for botanical names. The article explains that plant names often arrive in inconsistent formats from various sources, such as spreadsheets, nursery catalogs, and user input, with issues like incorrect symbols (x instead of ×), misspelled abbrevi

item.title: GOP Concerns Grow as Trump Support Erodes Among Kansas Voters
item.description: The article discusses growing unease within the Republican Party, particularly in Kansas, as voters begin to distance themselves from President Donald Trump's policies and leadership. According to the Washington Post, many Republicans are privately expressing concerns about Trump's economic record and foreign policy, but remain publicly loyal until they feel it's safe to speak out. Kris Clark, a 40-year-old software engineer from Olathe, Kansas, notes that extreme Trump supporters are hesitant to backtrack on their support due to fear of appearing foolish. This sentiment is reflected in the political landscape, where Senator Roger Marshall's once-safe reelection bid has become competitive against Democrat Adam Hamilton, a founding pastor of the United Methodist Church of the Resurrection. item.description: U.S. Representative Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) has been accused of spreading defamatory statements after falsely claiming that Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed advocated for Sharia law and progressive activist Hasan Piker promoted sexual assault. item.description: The article discusses the growing conflict between President Donald Trump and various lawmakers regarding the expansion of data centers in the United States. Trump has strongly supported the development of data centers, arguing they are essential for maintaining U.S. leadership in the artificial intelligence (AI) race and boosting economic growth. However, Democratic lawmakers are calling for stricter regulations on data centers, citing concerns about water usage, electricity costs, and community impacts. Representative Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) has urged Arizona to pause data center expansion until the state can assess long-term environmental and economic impacts, particularly regarding water preservation and ratepayer responsibilities. Robert Garcia (D-CA), is investigating the financial involvement of Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev in a celebration tied to Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding. item.description: Texas Republicans are experiencing internal conflict following controversial remarks made by GOP nominee Bo French, who posted a photo of University of Texas football fans, predominantly people of color, with a comment suggesting the issue was 'far worse than anyone imagined.' The post, which targeted South Asian students, has sparked a firestorm within the party, with Governor Greg Abbott attempting to distance himself by stating the remarks were not his message. item.title: Meta Introduces Subscription Model for AI Photo-Editing Tools on Instagram
item.description: Meta is implementing a subscription model for its AI photo-editing tools on Instagram, requiring users to pay for enhanced features. The company has introduced Meta One Core, a subscription tier priced at $7.99 per month, which unlocks additional AI effects and other perks. The article details the author's experience testing the new feature, where after using the free AI tools for a limited number of edits, a paywall appeared prompting users to upgrade to Meta One Core. item.title: The Ovitz Family: A Group of Dwarfs Who Survived Auschwitz Through Medical Experiments
item.description: The Ovitz family was a Jewish family of performers from Transylvania, Romania, known as the Liliput Troupe. Comprising ten siblings, seven of whom had pseudoachondroplasia, they toured Europe performing music and comedy before World War II. When the Nazis invaded, their unique physical characteristics saved them from immediate extermination at Auschwitz, but subjected them to pseudo-scientific abuse. In May 1944, the Ovitz family was deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau. Upon arrival, their appearance caught the attention of camp officers, who alerted Dr. Josef Mengele. Mengele, fascinated by genetics and hereditary anomalies, spared all 12 family members (including average-height relatives and pseudo-relatives they claimed as kin) from the gas chambers to conduct medical experiments on them. item.title: Georgia Police Seek Man Who Trespassed, Stole Towels, and Interacted with Rubber Duck in Hot Tub

item.title: Buzkashi: The Ancient and Fierce Traditional Sport of Tajikistan
item.description: Buzkashi, known as 'goat pulling' in Persian, is an ancient and fiercely contested sport deeply rooted in Tajikistan's cultural heritage. The sport, which has been played for centuries among the nomadic horse cultures of Central Asia, involves riders competing to seize and hold the headless carcass of a goat, aiming to drag it across a goal line marked by scattered hay. Unlike modern team sports, Buzkashi has no formal teams, boundaries, or referees, creating a chaotic and mythic spectacle that echoes historical cavalry charges. The game is played in vast open fields, often in remote valleys, and is central to Tajik cultural gatherings such as weddings, seasonal festivals, and rites of passage. It is not merely preserved as a heritage activity but is actively lived and experienced by the community. item.title: Vitamin D Deficiency Linked to Increased Postoperative Pain and Opioid Use in Breast Cancer Surgery Patients
item.description: A recent study published in Regional Anesthesia & Pain Medicine has revealed a significant association between low vitamin D levels and increased postoperative pain and opioid consumption in breast cancer patients undergoing mastectomy. The research, conducted at Fayoum University Hospital in Egypt between September 2024 and April 2025, involved 184 women scheduled for unilateral modified radical mastectomy. The study found that patients with vitamin D deficiency (below 30 nmol/L) were three times more likely to experience moderate to severe pain during the first 24 hours after surgery compared to those with sufficient vitamin D levels (above 30 nmol/L). item.title: Bryan Adams' 2007 Photo Session with Amy Winehouse Captured Her Signature Style and Emotional Depth
item.description: The article discusses a photo session featuring Amy Winehouse photographed by Bryan Adams in April 2007 for Zoo Magazine. The session took place in Los Angeles, California, as Winehouse's album 'Back to Black' was dominating global charts. Adams, who co-founded Zoo Magazine in 2003, captured Winehouse in a series of striking, raw portraits that highlighted her distinct retro style, signature tattoos, and intense emotion. item.title: Andy Goldsworthy's Autumn Leaf Art: A Timeless Practice of Nature's Palette
item.description: Andy Goldsworthy, a renowned artist known for his ephemeral works in nature, has spent four decades working with autumn leaves to create intricate, colorful arrangements that exist only for a short time. The article explains that Goldsworthy's process involves gathering fallen leaves, sorting them by color, and arranging them in gradients or patterns that highlight the natural beauty of the season. He does not add any pigments or materials; instead, he simply organizes what is already present on the ground. The work is temporary, lasting only as long as the weather permits, and the only permanent record is the photograph taken during the brief period when the arrangement is intact. Goldsworthy's approach emphasizes the fleeting nature of autumn, where the vibrant colors of leaves are quickly lost to rain, wind, and decay. item.title: Pennsylvania Reports Third Measles-Related Death as Outbreak Continues
item.description:
Pennsylvania officials have reported the state's third death related to measles, marking a significant development in the ongoing outbreak. The deceased, a 40-year-old woman from Jefferson County, died on Saturday due to complications from measles, according to Jefferson County Coroner Greg Furlong. Furlong described the death as 'measles-related' in a Facebook post, though he did not disclose whether the woman had been vaccinated against measles. The post also stated that no further details about the case would be released.
This marks the third measles-related death in Pennsylvania this year. The two previous deaths involved infants: one a newborn boy who died shortly after birth from a ruptured spleen, with measles listed as a 'significant condition' at the time of death, and another a 6-week-old girl with Amish lethal microcephaly, a genetic condition that left her highly vulnerable to infections, who died directly from measles. item.description: President Donald Trump announced on social media that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking each other's energy infrastructure. In a post signed 'President DJT,' Trump stated, 'Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!' However, he provided no details on how or when the agreement was reached, who brokered it, or what mechanism would enforce it. item.description: The article details the growing despair among Gazans following statements by Israeli officials that contradict a proposed peace plan for Gaza. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have both rejected the Board of Peace's roadmap, which includes Hamas disarming, Gaza demilitarizing, and a gradual Israeli withdrawal. item.title: Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson, Architect of Failed Tax Experiment, Runs for Governor
item.description: The article details the political and financial history surrounding Kansas Governor Sam Brownback's tax experiment, which aimed to eliminate the state income tax. The plan, enacted in 2012 by Republican lawmakers, led to four years of unbalanced budgets, unfair tax increases, and historic debt. Current gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson, who was the primary beneficiary of the ouster of moderate Republican leaders in the 2012 primary elections, played a key role in the execution of the failed tax experiment. Masterson, as chair of the Senate Ways and Means Committee, oversaw state finance and kept the failing tax experiment on life support despite plummeting revenues. The committee signed off on deficit spending that reduced general fund balances from $709 million in 2013 to $37 million in 2016. item.description: The race for California's next superintendent of public instruction has become a hyper-partisan contest between Democrat Richard Barrera, backed by the California Teachers Association (CTA), and Republican Sonja Shaw, aligned with MAGA and conservative education movements. Despite Democratic lawmakers recently stripping many powers from the superintendent role, the election remains a critical bellwether for California's educational policies and its stance against Trump-era federal education policies. Barrera, a union organizer with a background in labor politics, emphasizes improving student performance, raising teacher salaries, and building environmentally sustainable schools through union labor. item.title: Retired General Challenges '60 Minutes' Defense of Defense Secretary Amid Military Arsenal Concerns
item.description: Retired United States Army Lieutenant General Mark Hertling critically examined the defense provided by Admiral Brad Cooper on '60 Minutes' regarding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Admiral Cooper, who serves as Central Command (CENTCOM) head, had defended Hegseth during a segment that faced significant criticism. Cooper claimed that the military was 'well armed and ready for any contingency' despite reports of shortages in missile stockpiles. Hertling, however, pointed out that while CENTCOM might be operationally capable, the strategic sustainability of the U.S. military is at risk. He stated that the U.S. has burned through a significant portion of its missile inventory, which affects other global regions including Asia, Europe, and North Korea. Hertling emphasized that domestic production capabilities cannot quickly replenish these losses. item.description: Five Missouri voters have filed a proposed class-action lawsuit seeking approximately $80 million from Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, alleging he violated state law in handling a referendum challenging Missouri's gerrymandered congressional map. The lawsuit, filed in Cole County Circuit Court, asks a judge to allow the plaintiffs to represent about 162,000 registered Missouri voters whose signatures were verified by local election authorities on the referendum petition. The case centers on a Missouri law requiring the secretary of state to pay between $100 and $500 to an aggrieved person if they 'neglect or refuse to perform any of the duties enjoined on him by law.' The plaintiffs are seeking the maximum $500 per person, totaling about $80 million. The lawsuit points to Hoskins' actions during the legal battle over the congressional map passed by Republican lawmakers in a 2025 special legislative session. item.description: The CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman, have issued stark warnings about the need to slow the pace of AI development to address safety risks, potentially disrupting the AI stock market they helped build. item.title: GOP Senator's Bank Board Membership Raises Ethics Concerns Amid Campaign Contributions
item.description: The Ohio Capital Journal has reported on the ethical concerns surrounding Jon Husted, a former lieutenant governor and current U.S. Senator, who joined the board of Heartland Bank in 2022 while holding two state positions. Husted, who was appointed to the U.S. Senate in 2025 by Governor Mike DeWine, received significant campaign contributions from Heartland Bank to his political committee, totaling $492,000 after he joined the bank's board. The contributions continued even after his Senate appointment, with the latest being $15,000 as of June 30, 2026. Husted's financial disclosures reveal that he and his wife had over $250,000 in deposits at the bank and $16,000 in stock of the bank's successor company. The Ohio Ethics Commission stated that campaign contributions are not considered a conflict of interest under state law unless there is evidence of bribery, fraud, or criminal activity. item.title: Back-to-School Season Brings Rise in Common Colds, Flu, and Other Respiratory Illnesses, Doctors Report
item.description: As students return to classrooms after summer break, healthcare professionals are reporting a surge in respiratory illnesses across the United States. According to multiple doctors cited in the article, common colds caused by rhinovirus and parainfluenza, as well as increased cases of COVID-19, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, influenza, and strep throat, are becoming more prevalent. Dr. Alexa Mieses Malchuk, a family physician in Pennsylvania, notes that respiratory viruses are already on the rise. Dr. Richard Martinello, chief medical officer of Yale Medicine, explains that respiratory tract infections often present with symptoms like cough, runny nose, congestion, sore throat, sneezing, and fever. The article highlights that rhinovirus is the most common cause of colds, while parainfluenza typically causes mild upper respiratory infections. item.title: Michel Molinari: A Mid-Century Fashion Photographer Known for Intimate Portraiture
item.description: Michel Molinari (1923-1997), often referred to as Michel Molinare, was a British fashion photographer active from the mid-1950s to the 1960s. Born in London and raised partly on the Italian Riviera, Molinari developed a distinctive style that combined classical sensitivity with a naturalistic approach. Working for prominent magazines such as Tatler, Harper's Bazaar, and Queen, Molinari created atmospheric images that captured a quiet closeness with his models. His work, often compared to the observational quality of Cartier-Bresson, favored authenticity and subtle expression over heavy artifice, leaving a refined record of postwar fashion photography. The article features numerous examples of Molinari's work from Harper's Bazaar UK, showcasing models in various fashion ensembles from the 1960s. item.description: The MV Matui ferry sank in rough seas off Vanuatu on Friday morning, resulting in a tragic disaster with over 30 people still missing and a confirmed death toll of two. The ferry departed from Santo at 6 a.m. for Ambae, approximately 96 kilometers away, but capsized in large waves around 9:30 a.m. The rescue operation faced significant delays due to confusion about the vessel's status and misinformation, with help not arriving for over 30 hours. Australian pilot and doctor Mark Turnbull, who assisted in the search, described the situation as 'a miracle anyone survived,' noting that survivors clung to floating debris including fuel drums, life jackets, and a large agricultural tank. item.description: Oracle co-founder and executive chairman Larry Ellison has canceled a planned sale of his Oracle stock, the company announced on Saturday. Oracle had previously disclosed in a regulatory filing that Ellison planned to sell 50 million shares worth around $7.5 billion, according to Reuters. The company did not offer a reason for the change in plans. 'No Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock,' the company said. item.description: Ben Shelton, the 23-year-old American tennis player, fell short in the U.S. Open final to Alexander Zverev of Germany, losing in four sets. Despite the loss, Shelton emerged as the standout player of the tournament, becoming the first Black man to reach a U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972 and the first American man to reach the final since Andy Roddick in 2003. Shelton's powerful serve, athleticism, and aggressive style captivated fans throughout the tournament, earning him widespread popularity. item.title: Queen Victoria's 1900 Chocolate Gift to Boer War Soldiers: A Historical Artifact Preserved for Over a Century
item.description: In late 1899, Queen Victoria commissioned Cadbury chocolates to be sent to over 100,000 British soldiers serving in South Africa during the Second Boer War (1899-1902) as a morale-boosting gift for the New Year of 1900. The British chocolate industry at the time was dominated by Quaker families—Cadbury, Fry, and Rowntree—who were strict pacifists opposed to the war. Initially, they refused to accept payment or brand the tins for war efforts. However, they eventually compromised by producing the chocolate for free, packaging it in unbranded or minimally marked tins. The tins featured a profile portrait of Queen Victoria, her royal monogram (VRI for Victoria Regina Imperatrix), and the inscription: 'I wish you a happy New Year - Victoria RI' alongside 'South Africa 1900'. Many soldiers cherished the tins as personal tokens from the Monarch and refused to eat the chocolate, leading to several intact bars surviving inside their original packaging for over a century. item.title: NASA-Backed Researchers Develop Protein-Rich Cookies from Plastic Waste and Agricultural Byproducts
item.description: Scientists at Southern Illinois University (SIU) Carbondale, supported by NASA, have engineered yeast to convert PET plastic and agricultural waste into protein-rich, 3D-printed cookies known as µBites. This innovative approach, developed partly for NASA's Deep Space Food Challenge, aims to address both plastic pollution and food insecurity while providing sustenance in extreme environments such as space missions. The process involves breaking down plastic and agricultural waste using a proprietary technique called oxidative hydrothermal dissolution, which combines water and oxygen under high temperature and pressure. The resulting compounds are then fed to genetically engineered yeast, which transforms them into proteins, fats, vitamins, and flavorings. These ingredients are combined with fiber, starch, and sweeteners to create µBites, which are currently being evaluated for safety and taste. item.title: Quantum-Enhanced Electron Microscopy: New Approach to Image Delicate Biological Samples with Fewer Electrons
item.description:
Scientists from TU Wien, in collaboration with researchers from the University of Vienna, JKU Linz, and the University of Innsbruck, are developing a groundbreaking technique that combines electron microscopy with quantum computing. The innovative approach aims to extract additional information from electrons used in imaging, potentially allowing researchers to create clearer images while exposing delicate biological samples to fewer electrons. This could significantly reduce damage to sensitive materials such as proteins and other biological specimens that are typically damaged by conventional electron microscopy.
The research team, led by Philipp Haslinger from TU Wien's Institute of Atomic and Subatomic Physics, explains that conventional electron microscopes primarily count electrons to build images, but each electron carries quantum information that is typically unused. item.title: British Artist George Owen Wynne Apperley Captured the Essence of Spain and Morocco Through His Romantic Paintings
item.description: George Owen Wynne Apperley (1884–1960) was a British painter associated with the late Romantic tradition. Born on the Isle of Wight, Apperley trained briefly at the Herkomer School before developing a largely self-taught style. In 1917, he moved to Spain, settling in Granada’s Albaicín district, where he became known for his atmospheric portraits, landscapes, and figurative works inspired by local life and Mediterranean light. Political tensions later forced him to leave for Tangier, Morocco, where he continued to paint until his death. Celebrated for his refined technique and romantic sensibility, Apperley is remembered as one of the distinctive British artists who made their careers in Spain and North Africa. item.title: Global Survey Reveals Deep Disagreements Among Physicists on Fundamental Cosmic Questions
item.description: A massive worldwide survey of physicists has revealed surprisingly little agreement about some of the universe's biggest mysteries. The study, conducted by researchers from the University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute, found that no majority backed the standard cosmological model (ΛCDM), a leading explanation for dark matter, or any single theory of quantum gravity. Only two areas showed majority agreement: 68% of physicists stated that the Big Bang does not necessarily represent the beginning of time, and 51% agreed that cosmic inflation occurred in the early universe. The survey also highlighted significant divisions on dark matter, with only 17% supporting the idea that dark matter consists of undiscovered low-mass particles, while 21% favored a combination of proposed explanations. item.title: New Study Reveals 3D Genome Organization Changes in Alzheimer's Disease
item.description: A groundbreaking study led by researchers from Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Washington has uncovered a previously unexplored layer of Alzheimer's disease related to the three-dimensional organization of DNA in brain cells. Published in the journal Science, the research demonstrates that the 3D structure of the genome is disrupted in several types of brain cells affected by Alzheimer's, altering how important genes are switched on and off. This discovery reveals a fundamental regulatory layer that connects DNA sequence to gene activity, moving beyond the traditional focus on amyloid-beta plaques and tau tangles, which are the classic hallmarks of the disease. The team used advanced techniques including GAGE-seq, which measures both gene expression and three-dimensional genome contacts within the same cell, combined with spatial transcriptomic maps to preserve information about where gene activity occurs within intact brain tissue. item.title: Jacqueline Bisset: A Career Spanning Decades in Film and Photography
item.description: Jacqueline Bisset, born September 13, 1944, is a British actress who began her film career in 1965 and gained prominence in 1968 with roles in The Detective, Bullitt, and The Sweet Ride, earning a Golden Globe nomination as Most Promising Newcomer. She transitioned from a 1960s and 1970s international sex symbol to a respected dramatic actress by the 1980s. Bisset starred in Airport (1970), one of the highest-grossing films of the decade, and worked with European auteur François Truffaut in Day for Night (1973), which won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Her role in The Deep (1977) became iconic, with an underwater scene wearing a thin white T-shirt that popularized the wet T-shirt trend worldwide. Despite media focus on her appearance, Bisset expressed frustration over the lack of attention to her acting. item.description: President Donald Trump announced the removal of a 15% tariff on Irish whisky that he had imposed in April 2025. The decision came after Trump attended the Irish Open trophy ceremony at the Trump International Golf Links & Hotel in Doonbeg, Ireland. During a press conference at Shannon Airport before returning to the U.S., Trump stated that the tariff was 'pretty unfair' because other countries had received relief. He mentioned that he discussed the tariff with professional golfer Shane Lowry, the winner of the Irish Open, who had raised the issue with him. item.title: Rare Whale Shark Sighted Off Southern California Coast During El Niño Event
item.description: A rare whale shark was recently spotted off the coast of Malibu, California, between Malibu and Santa Barbara Island, according to a report by the Los Angeles Times. The sighting was captured on video by Carl Sbarounis, a Southern California pilot and commercial fisherman, who documented the 14- to 16-foot-long whale shark cruising through the Pacific Ocean. Sbarounis, who has been spotting marine life for over 40 years, noted that whale sharks typically appear during warm water conditions, such as those associated with El Niño events. The whale shark, the largest fish in the world, feeds on plankton and has small teeth, making it harmless to humans. The sighting occurred during a period of regional marine heatwave, which has been warming the waters along the Southern California coast. This is not the first unusual marine sighting this summer; in August, a hammerhead shark was also spotted near Malibu. item.title: Linda Harrison: The Actress Behind Nova in 'Planet of the Apes' and Her Enduring Legacy
item.description: Linda Harrison, born in 1945, is an American actress best known for her role as Nova in the 1968 science-fiction film 'Planet of the Apes' and its 1970 sequel 'Beneath the Planet of the Apes.' Harrison, a former beauty pageant winner from Maryland, was signed by 20th Century Fox and quickly became one of the studio's rising stars in the late 1960s. Despite having almost no dialogue in the films, Harrison conveyed deep emotion and presence through her expressions and physicality, creating one of the most memorable images of the original 'Planet of the Apes' series. Her performance as Nova, a character who communicates primarily through non-verbal means, has left a lasting impact on popular culture. Harrison remains closely associated with the film and is celebrated as a distinctive face of late-1960s Hollywood. On Friday, the Iran-backed Houthi militants captured Mayyun Island, which divides the Bab al-Mandab Strait—a critical global shipping route—into two channels. This follows their earlier control of Yemen's west coast along the same strategic waterway. The Houthis had previously blocked Saudi Arabian oil shipments through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, and with their new territorial control, traversing the waterway has become 'very risky' unless the Houthis permit it, warned security analyst Wolfgang Pusztai. Pusztai also noted that Iran benefits from this development, gaining additional leverage over another global chokepoint and making its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz more effective. item.title: Dave Mustaine's Early Band Panic: Tragic Losses and the Path to Metallica
item.description: Before joining Metallica in late 1981, a teenage Dave Mustaine formed his very first group, Panic, in Southern California around 1980. Though short-lived and plagued by tragedy, Panic was where Mustaine developed his aggressive lead guitar style and wrote early riffs that eventually shaped thrash metal history. The original lineup included Dave Harmon on drums, Tom Queck on guitar, Bob Evans on bass, Pat Voeks as singer, and Mustaine on lead guitar. The band was short-lived, with members rarely performing and rehearsing, especially in late 1980 and 1981, as the band began to break up. They mostly went to parties, jammed a little, and hung out with girls. Mustaine recalled a talent show where they were kicked out for being too loud, and his first gig with Panic at Huntington Beach. However, the band's history was marred by the death of two friends: the sound engineer Joe and drummer Dave Harmon, who died in a car accident. item.title: The Pacific Ocean's Remote Spacecraft Graveyard: A Point of Isolation
item.description: The article discusses the Point Nemo, a location in the South Pacific Ocean that is the farthest point from any landmass on Earth. Named after Jules Verne's character 'Nemo', this point is approximately 2,688 kilometers from the nearest land, which includes the Pitcairn Islands, Easter Island, and Antarctica. The area is known as the 'spacecraft graveyard' because it has been used as a disposal site for decommissioned spacecraft and space stations since 1971. Over 250 spacecraft, including the Mir space station and several Soviet stations, have been deliberately crashed into the ocean near Point Nemo. The article notes that the International Space Station (ISS) is also scheduled to be deorbited into this area within the next decade. Point Nemo is extremely remote, with no human settlements, minimal marine life, and no shipping or air routes passing nearby. The shop focuses on small, beautifully designed objects that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing. item.title: Claudette Colbert's Career Transition in the 1950s: From Hollywood to Broadway and Television
item.description: Claudette Colbert, born on September 13, 1903, and passing away on July 30, 1996, experienced a significant career shift during the 1950s. Initially a prominent figure in Hollywood films, she gradually moved away from mainstream cinema as her box-office appeal diminished. Colbert leveraged her early theater background to successfully transition into television and Broadway stage roles. The role was subsequently given to Bette Davis, who delivered an iconic performance. item.title: Mercury's Shrinkage Exceeds Previous Estimates, Study Reveals
item.description: A recent study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters has revealed that Mercury may have shrunk approximately 30% more than previously estimated, losing up to 14 miles in diameter over billions of years as its interior cooled and contracted. The research, led by Gaku Nishiyama, suggests that Mercury's rough surface, continually reshaped by debris from impact craters, may have obscured the true extent of the planet's contraction. This finding is particularly significant given Mercury's relatively small size, measuring barely 3,000 miles (4,900 kilometers) across. The study's findings come just one week after the European and Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo, which are currently en route to Mercury, detached from their cruise stage and are expected to enter orbit around the planet in November. item.description: LG has issued a response to recent allegations that its smart TVs are 'spying' on users, clarifying that wake-word detection occurs locally on the device and that features such as Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), voice recognition, and interest-based advertising are optional. The company emphasized that speech-to-text processing only begins when a user activates a voice interaction through a supported wake-word feature or by pressing the voice (or AI) button on the remote control. item.title: Quantum Interferometer Tests Equivalence Principle in Free Fall
item.description: A team of physicists led by Ron Folman from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev has successfully conducted an experiment that tests the interaction between quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory of relativity. The researchers developed a new type of interferometer called the Quantum Galileo Interferometer (QGI) that places atoms in a superposition of trajectories—one involving free fall and the other where the atom remains stationary. This experiment is significant because it represents the first time the equivalence principle, a cornerstone of Einstein's theory of relativity, has been tested in a quantum system. The experiment involved cooling rubidium atoms to near absolute zero and using microwave and magnetic pulses to create a superposition of states. item.title: Heart Calcium Scans Most Beneficial for Patients with Intermediate Risk, Study Finds
item.description: A 10-year study involving over 6,000 adults conducted by Northwestern University has revealed that coronary artery calcium scans may not significantly improve heart disease risk prediction for most people when compared to standard risk assessment tools. However, for those in the intermediate risk category (3% to 9% risk of heart disease within 10 years), the calcium scan offered meaningful improvements in predicting future cardiovascular events. The study tracked participants aged 45 to 79 over a decade, with 6% experiencing heart attacks or strokes during that period. item.title: Scientists Discover New Ice Structure Under Extreme Conditions, Resembling Planetary Interiors
item.description: Scientists have successfully created and observed a new form of ice under extreme conditions, marking a significant breakthrough in understanding planetary science. The research, led by physicist Alexis Forestier from the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission, involved subjecting tiny water samples to pressures up to 230 gigapascals (2.3 million atmospheres) and temperatures reaching 2,630 kelvins (2,357 degrees Celsius). These conditions mimic the interior environments of ice giant planets like Uranus and Neptune. Using diamond anvils to compress the samples and lasers to heat them, researchers probed the crystal structure with synchrotron X-rays. The resulting ice structure, hexagonal close-packed (hcp) ice, had been theoretically predicted but never conclusively observed in experiments. item.description: The New England Journal of Medicine Clinician Review discusses a study examining the necessity of annual MRI scans for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) treated with ocrelizumab. item.description: The article discusses the technical intricacies of ensuring provable fairness in cryptographic systems, particularly focusing on the critical need for the browser-based verifier to match the server's arithmetic operations exactly, bit for bit. Both the server (written in Kotlin) and the browser verifier (written in JavaScript) use 64-bit doubles with 53 bits of precision, but a hash contains more bits than can be precisely represented. The problem occurs when rounding happens multiple times during conversion versus a single rounding, which can cause discrepancies in the final outcome, such as a game multiplying the number by 37 and rounding down landing in a different pocket. item.description: According to a recent report published in JAMA Pediatrics, suicide rates among girls aged 10-14 have increased at a faster rate than boys in recent years, making suicide the second leading cause of death in this age group in the United States. The report, authored by Dr. Jean Twenge, a psychology professor at San Diego State University, identifies social media use and the impact of COVID-19 lockdowns as key factors contributing to this trend. Dr. Twenge notes that from 2010 to 2019, social media and smartphones were largely responsible for the rise in suicide rates, particularly among girls. She explains that social media use is more strongly linked to depression and mental health issues in girls compared to boys, with girls experiencing heightened pressure related to physical appearance and online validation through likes and followers. item.title: Trump's Proposed Census Changes Challenge Constitutional Rights, Experts Warn
item.description: The Washington Post Editorial Board has published an opinion piece warning that President Donald Trump's proposed changes to the U.S. census would violate the Constitution, specifically the 14th Amendment. The article notes that Trump was previously foiled in his first administration when attempting to alter the census, which determines each state's representation in Congress. This week, Trump has reignited the battle over census changes, setting up a fresh conflict that experts believe he will likely lose again. The 14th Amendment guarantees equal protection under the law and requires that representation in Congress be based on the total population, including all residents regardless of citizenship status. The proposed changes would involve willfully excluding millions of people from the 2030 census count, which would directly contradict the constitutional mandate.
